---
title: "Simulated test dataset: one function across remote homologs"
subtitle: "GrpE (COG0576) spiked into group A, one 30% cluster per sample"
bibliography: references.bib
link-citations: true
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Design.** 20 samples, 10 in group A and 10 in group B. All samples share
100 background proteins drawn at random from other COGs. Each group-A sample
also carries one GrpE protein (COG0576) of its own, and the 10 GrpE proteins
come from 10 different MMseqs2 30% clusters [@steinegger2017mmseqs2]. So
group A is enriched for one function, while no sequence family is enriched
in more than one sample. The FASTA therefore holds 110 proteins (100 + 10);
an A sample has 101, a B sample 100.

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Treatment COG | COG0576, GrpE |
| Samples | 10 A + 10 B |
| Background proteins (all samples) | 100 |
| GrpE proteins (one per A sample) | 10, from 10 different 30% clusters |
| Perturbation $\rho$ (GrpE share in its A sample) | 5% |
| Depth | $2 \times 10^4$ |
| Seed | `20261112` (proteins), `1` (counts) |

```{r params}
treatment_cog <- "COG0576"
n_per_group <- 10L
n_background <- 100L
rho <- 0.05
depth <- 2e4
length_range <- c(50L, 1000L)
cog_dir <- file.path("data", "cog")
out_dir <- "data_simulation"
dir.create(cog_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# 1. Source: NCBI COG 2024

The COG 2024 release [@galperin2025cog]: protein-to-COG assignments, the
protein sequences of its 2,296 genomes, COG names and functional categories.
About 2.2 GB, downloaded once into `data/cog/` and checked against the
release's MD5 sums.

```{r download}
base <- "https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/pub/COG/COG2024/data/"
files <- c("checksums.md5", "cog-24.def.tab", "cog-24.fun.tab", "cog-24.cog.csv",
    "COGorg24.faa.gz")
for (f in files) {
    p <- file.path(cog_dir, f)
    if (!file.exists(p)) curl::curl_download(paste0(base, f), p)
}
md5 <- read.table(file.path(cog_dir, "checksums.md5"), col.names = c("md5", "file"))
md5 <- md5[md5$file %in% files, ]
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(cog_dir, md5$file))), md5$md5))
```

# 2. One-label pool

A protein qualifies if it has exactly one COG, every assignment row for it
is membership class 0 (the COG covers most of the protein and most of the
COG profile, so the label is full-length), and it is 50-1000 residues long.

```{r pool}
a <- read.csv(file.path(cog_dir, "cog-24.cog.csv"), header = FALSE,
    colClasses = c("NULL", "NULL", "character", "integer", "NULL", "NULL",
        "character", "NULL", "integer", rep("NULL", 4)))
names(a) <- c("protein", "length", "cog", "class")
pc <- unique(a[c("protein", "cog")])
multi <- unique(pc$protein[duplicated(pc$protein)])
pool <- unique(a[!a$protein %in% c(multi, a$protein[a$class != 0L]),
    c("protein", "length", "cog")])
pool <- pool[pool$length >= length_range[1] & pool$length <= length_range[2], ]
rm(a, pc)
c(proteins = nrow(pool), COGs = length(unique(pool$cog)),
    GrpE = sum(pool$cog == treatment_cog))
```

# 3. Sequences

All GrpE proteins, plus 300 random background candidates (slack for the
filters below), are read from the release FASTA. Sequences must use the 20
standard residues; identical sequences keep the lowest protein id.

```{r sequences}
set.seed(20261112L)
bg_cand <- pool[pool$cog != treatment_cog, ]
bg_cand <- bg_cand[sample.int(nrow(bg_cand), 3L * n_background), ]
cand <- rbind(pool[pool$cog == treatment_cog, ], bg_cand)
ids <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
fa <- tempfile(fileext = ".fa")
writeLines(cand$protein, ids)
stopifnot(system(sprintf(paste("gzip -dc %s | awk 'NR==FNR {k[$1]; next}",
    "/^>/ {p = (substr($1, 2) in k)} p' %s - > %s"),
    shQuote(file.path(cog_dir, "COGorg24.faa.gz")), shQuote(ids), shQuote(fa))) == 0L)
s <- Biostrings::readAAStringSet(fa)
keep <- !duplicated(sub(" .*", "", names(s)))
s <- s[keep]
hdr <- names(s)
names(s) <- sub(" .*", "", hdr)
cand$sequence <- as.character(s)[cand$protein]
cand$organism <- sub(".*\\[(.*)\\]$", "\\1", hdr[match(cand$protein, names(s))])
cand <- cand[!is.na(cand$sequence) & grepl("^[ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+$", cand$sequence), ]
cand <- cand[order(cand$protein), ]
cand <- cand[!duplicated(cand$sequence), ]
table(role = ifelse(cand$cog == treatment_cog, "GrpE", "background candidate"))
```

# 4. GrpE: one protein from each of 10 different 30% clusters

Every qualifying GrpE protein is clustered with MMseqs2 at 30% identity and
80% coverage of both sequences (`-s 7.5`, the settings of the other
simulations). Clusters are visited in random order and one random member is
taken from each, but only if it has no alignment of $\ge$ 30% identity over
70% of both proteins with a GrpE protein already taken. Greedy clustering
depends on which sequences are present, so this pairwise rule is what keeps
the 10 in 10 clusters when clustered with the background; the margin (70%,
not 80%) is there because `easy-search` and `easy-cluster` align slightly
differently (one pair at 48% identity covered 76-79% in the search but was
clustered together).

```{r mmseqs}
mmseqs_cluster <- function(seqs) {
    tmp <- tempfile("mm")
    dir.create(tmp)
    f <- file.path(tmp, "x.fasta")
    Biostrings::writeXStringSet(Biostrings::AAStringSet(seqs), f)
    stopifnot(system2("mmseqs", c("easy-cluster", f, file.path(tmp, "c"), file.path(tmp, "w"),
        "--min-seq-id", 0.3, "-c", 0.8, "--cov-mode", 0, "--cluster-mode", 0, "-s", 7.5),
        stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) == 0L)
    m <- read.delim(file.path(tmp, "c_cluster.tsv"), header = FALSE)
    unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE)
    setNames(m$V1, m$V2)[names(seqs)]
}
mmseqs_search <- function(seqs) {
    tmp <- tempfile("mm")
    dir.create(tmp)
    f <- file.path(tmp, "x.fasta")
    Biostrings::writeXStringSet(Biostrings::AAStringSet(seqs), f)
    stopifnot(system2("mmseqs", c("easy-search", f, f, file.path(tmp, "h.m8"),
        file.path(tmp, "w"), "-s", 7.5, "-e", "1e-3", "--max-seqs", 10000,
        "--format-output", "query,target,fident,qcov,tcov,evalue"),
        stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) == 0L)
    h <- read.delim(file.path(tmp, "h.m8"), header = FALSE,
        col.names = c("query", "target", "fident", "qcov", "tcov", "evalue"))
    unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE)
    h[h$query != h$target, ]
}
grpe <- cand[cand$cog == treatment_cog, ]
grpe$c30 <- mmseqs_cluster(setNames(grpe$sequence, grpe$protein))
c(GrpE = nrow(grpe), clusters_30pct = length(unique(grpe$c30)))
hits <- mmseqs_search(setNames(grpe$sequence, grpe$protein))
hits <- hits[hits$fident >= 0.3 & hits$qcov >= 0.7 & hits$tcov >= 0.7, ]
close <- c(paste(hits$query, hits$target), paste(hits$target, hits$query))
set.seed(20261112L)
taken <- character()
for (cl in sample(unique(grpe$c30))) {
    m <- grpe$protein[grpe$c30 == cl]
    p <- m[sample.int(length(m), 1L)]
    if (!any(paste(p, taken) %in% close)) taken <- c(taken, p)
    if (length(taken) == n_per_group) break
}
stopifnot(length(taken) == n_per_group)
treat <- grpe[match(taken, grpe$protein), ]
treat$c30 <- NULL
```

# 5. Background: 100 random proteins

Background candidates with an MMseqs2 hit to any of the 10 GrpE proteins
(E $\le$ 10^-3^ and 80% coverage of both) are dropped, so no background
protein is a close homolog of the treatment; the first 100 remaining, in
the random order of the draw, are kept.

```{r background}
bg <- cand[cand$cog != treatment_cog, ]
bg <- bg[match(bg_cand$protein, bg$protein, nomatch = 0L), ]
h <- mmseqs_search(setNames(c(treat$sequence, bg$sequence), c(treat$protein, bg$protein)))
h <- h[h$qcov >= 0.8 & h$tcov >= 0.8, ]
leak <- unique(c(h$query[h$target %in% treat$protein], h$target[h$query %in% treat$protein]))
leak <- intersect(leak, bg$protein)
bg <- head(bg[!bg$protein %in% leak, ], n_background)
c(leak_removed = length(leak), background = nrow(bg), background_COGs = length(unique(bg$cog)))
```

# 6. Check: the 110 proteins at 30% identity

Clustered together, the 10 GrpE proteins must still fall in 10 different
30% clusters. The highest identity between any two of them (MMseqs2 local
alignments, E $\le$ 10^-3^) shows how remote they are.

```{r check}
treat$role <- "GrpE"
treat$enriched_in <- sprintf("A%02d", seq_len(n_per_group))
bg$role <- "background"
bg$enriched_in <- NA_character_
u <- rbind(treat, bg)
u$mmseqs30 <- unname(mmseqs_cluster(setNames(u$sequence, u$protein)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(u$mmseqs30[u$role == "GrpE"]))
hg <- mmseqs_search(setNames(treat$sequence, treat$protein))
c(GrpE_clusters = length(unique(u$mmseqs30[u$role == "GrpE"])),
    universe_clusters = length(unique(u$mmseqs30)),
    GrpE_pairs = choose(n_per_group, 2),
    GrpE_pairs_with_hit = length(unique(paste(pmin(hg$query, hg$target),
        pmax(hg$query, hg$target)))),
    max_GrpE_identity = if (nrow(hg)) max(hg$fident) else NA)
```

# 7. Functional labels and FASTA

```{r labels}
def <- read.delim(file.path(cog_dir, "cog-24.def.tab"), header = FALSE, quote = "",
    fileEncoding = "latin1", col.names = c("cog", "category", "name", "gene",
        "pathway", "pubmed", "pdb"))
fun <- read.delim(file.path(cog_dir, "cog-24.fun.tab"), header = FALSE, quote = "",
    col.names = c("category", "group", "color", "description"))
d <- def[match(u$cog, def$cog), ]
labels <- data.frame(protein = u$protein, role = u$role, enriched_in = u$enriched_in,
    cog = u$cog, cog_name = d$name, gene = d$gene, category = d$category,
    category_name = fun$description[match(substr(d$category, 1, 1), fun$category)],
    length = nchar(u$sequence), organism = u$organism, mmseqs30 = u$mmseqs30)
write.table(labels, file.path(out_dir, "labels.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE, na = "")
Biostrings::writeXStringSet(Biostrings::AAStringSet(setNames(u$sequence, u$protein)),
    file.path(out_dir, "proteins.fasta"))
knitr::kable(labels[labels$role == "GrpE", c("protein", "enriched_in", "length",
    "organism", "mmseqs30")], row.names = FALSE, caption = "The 10 GrpE proteins")
knitr::kable(head(sort(table(labels$category_name[labels$role == "background"]),
    decreasing = TRUE), 10), col.names = c("COG category", "background proteins"))
```

# 8. Count table

A negative-binomial model, as in the other simulations. Background
abundances $\pi$ are log-normal and shared by all samples; sample $i$ has
size factor $s_i \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.25)$ and protein $j$ has
dispersion $\phi_{ij} = (0.1 + 1/\mu_{ij})\, e_j$, $e_j \sim
\mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.5)$. Group-A sample $i$ puts a share $\rho = 5\%$ of
its abundance on its own GrpE protein and $1 - \rho$ on the background; group
B and every other GrpE protein get 0. The counts are drawn with seed 1.

```{r counts}
samples <- data.frame(sample = c(sprintf("A%02d", seq_len(n_per_group)),
    sprintf("B%02d", seq_len(n_per_group))), group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = n_per_group))
samples$grpe_protein <- treat$protein[match(samples$sample, treat$enriched_in)]
write.table(samples, file.path(out_dir, "samples.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE, na = "")
set.seed(20261112L)
pi <- setNames(rlnorm(nrow(bg)), bg$protein)
pi <- pi / sum(pi)
s <- rlnorm(nrow(samples), 0, 0.25)
e <- setNames(rlnorm(nrow(u), 0, 0.5), u$protein)
p <- matrix(0, nrow(samples), nrow(u), dimnames = list(samples$sample, u$protein))
p[, bg$protein] <- matrix(pi, nrow(samples), nrow(bg), byrow = TRUE)
a <- samples$group == "A"
p[a, ] <- (1 - rho) * p[a, ]
p[cbind(which(a), match(samples$grpe_protein[a], u$protein))] <- rho
mu <- s * depth * p
phi <- (0.1 + 1 / mu) * rep(e, each = nrow(samples))
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu = mu, size = 1 / phi), nrow(mu),
    dimnames = dimnames(mu))
counts[mu == 0] <- 0L # rnbinom gives NaN at mu = 0, size = 0
storage.mode(counts) <- "integer"
write.table(data.frame(sample = rownames(counts), counts, check.names = FALSE),
    file.path(out_dir, "counts.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
share <- rowSums(counts[a, treat$protein]) / rowSums(counts[a, ])
c(median_depth = median(rowSums(counts)), GrpE_share_in_A_median = median(share),
    GrpE_share_in_A_min = min(share), GrpE_share_in_A_max = max(share),
    GrpE_counts_in_B = sum(counts[!a, treat$protein]))
```

# Output files

```{r files}
f <- list.files(out_dir, full.names = TRUE)
data.frame(file = f, bytes = file.size(f))
```

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `proteins.fasta` | the 110 proteins |
| `labels.tsv` | protein, role (GrpE or background), the A sample it is spiked into, COG id, name, gene, functional category, length, organism, MMseqs2 30% cluster |
| `samples.tsv` | sample, group, its GrpE protein |
| `counts.tsv` | counts, samples × proteins |
